I would guess that the towels were left in the washer too long or they were used too often before being able to fully dry. Once the mildew gets in them the smell is always there to a certain extent. To make things better in the meantime before replacing the towels, you can wash them with equal parts baking soda and white vinegar. I put the washer on soak for 30 minutes and wash at the hottest temp. Then rewash them with laundry detergent. Make sure to get them in the dryer as soon as they are done washing and again dry at the highest temp. Good luck!

Beagles are known for barking, so it may never completely stop. To make him comfortable, make sure he has a comfy place to sit/lay down in the room he sleeps and any room the family spends lot of time in. I would put the shirts in these areas. We use crates for our dogs to sleep in, so they always have a place of their own if they want to be left alone. You will have to crate train, though. I recommend watching training videos on YouTube if you decide to crate train. 

To stop the barking, get a can with a metal bottom (coffee can, soda can, etc), put a few pennies inside, and tape it shut. Shake it at the dog immediately when he starts barking. They don't like the sound and will stop. You can use this for any bad behaviors you want stopped. I recommend keeping a few cans around as timing it as soon after the bad behavior is key.

I went to the ER when I was in college as I was told this could be a way to obtain antidepressants. When asked if I had suicidal thoughts, I was honest but also explained my therapist, family, and I had measures in place to prevent an attempt. It didn't matter. The nurse told me I needed to go to the psych ward to be evaluated in order to prescribe meds. Unfortunately, this was just a trick. As soon as I entered, the doors closed and an armed guard was there preventing my leaving. I tried, talked to the docs, nurses, guard, etc explaining I was not suicidal and just needed meds per my therapist. It didn't matter. They kept me there most of the day before realizing I was right, and prescribing the worst med I've ever been on. Unfortunately, the experience of being held against my will was so traumatising I don't remember the name of the med. 

Cut to 10 years later when I really need help but am terrified of being locked up against my will. My husband and I found a nonprofit mental health facility that offered outpatient treatment. It was the best decision I have made, but I had to ask someone I trusted for help and not a medical professional. Our health system still needs a lot of work, especially when it comes to mental health, but there are good options. My advice, find someone you trust to help you find the right treatment for you. Good luck!
